title: Complete summary – Retroperitoneum, adrenals & genital tract
html:
Built by reverse-engineering every MCQ of this lecture. 🔁 = asked in several sessions · ⚠ = classic trap.

Retroperitoneum

  • Retroperitoneal: kidneys & ureters, adrenals, pancreas, ascending & descending colon, aorta/IVC, inter-aortocaval lymph nodes.
  • Intraperitoneal (traps): stomach, spleen, transverse colon ⚠
  • Lymphadenopathy: short axis > 10 mm abnormal (retrocrural > 6 mm); round hypoechoic on US; lymphoma, metastases.
  • Best technique for retroperitoneal nodes: contrast-enhanced CT (separates nodes from vessels/bowel); US limited by gas and obesity.

Adrenal glands 🔁🔁🔁

  • Method of choice: CT (better than US); MRI chemical shift for characterisation when CT is inconclusive.
  • In obese patients, retroperitoneal fat HELPS CT (it is US that is limited) ⚠
  • Myelolipoma = the ONLY adrenal tumour with a specific appearance: macroscopic fat → hyperechoic on US and HYPOdense (negative HU) on CT. "Hyperechoic and hyperdense" is FALSE.
  • Adenoma: most frequent incidentaloma; lipid-rich < 10 HU on native CT; rapid contrast washout; signal drop on chemical-shift MRI; not always bilateral.
  • Bilateral adrenal tumours → metastases (lung, breast, melanoma); also bilateral hyperplasia, bilateral phaeochromocytoma (MEN), haemorrhage. Lung-cancer metastases are often bilateral and heterogeneous (not "unilateral hypodense").
  • Phaeochromocytoma: a negative US never rules it out (FALSE statement asked in the old exam and 2025) ⚠

Female pelvis 🔁🔁

  • Transvaginal US = first line (endometrium, ovaries). MRI = local staging (shows the junctional zone; T2 is the most reliable sequence). CT = distant metastases; omental cake visible on CT (not only MRI).
  • Doppler hypovascularity does NOT exclude malignancy; US cannot reliably assess pelvic nodes; a negative TVUS does not make MRI unnecessary.
  • Post-menopausal bleeding + endometrium > 4 mm (e.g. 8 mm) → endometrial biopsy.
  • Endometrial cancer FIGO on MRI: IA < 50 % myometrial invasion, IB ≥ 50 %, II cervical stroma, IVA bladder/rectal mucosa.
  • Leiomyoma (fibroid): hypoechoic well-delineated; hypointense T1 and T2; calcification, necrosis possible; CT not used.

Ovarian cysts

LesionImaging
Benign / simple cystanechoic, thin wall, no or thin septa, T1 hypo / T2 hyper; reliably diagnosed by US (IOTA)
Endometrioma"chocolate cyst" (homogeneous low-level echoes) → endometriosis; T1 fat-sat hyperintense, T2 intermediate / "shading"
Ovarian cancercyst-in-cyst, papillary projections, thick vascular septa, solid parts, ascites, omental caking; CT mainly for lymph node metastases

Prostate 🔁

  • Detection & staging of cancer: multiparametric MRI (PI-RADS), performed before biopsy; biopsy for PI-RADS 4–5 (consider 3), not PI-RADS 2; prostatitis ≠ PI-RADS 5.
  • Cancer mostly in the peripheral zone (~70 %); metastases are sclerotic (osteoblastic) → bone scan.
  • Best and most efficient method to assess the gland (volume, biopsy guidance): transrectal US. CT not for local staging.

Scrotum

  • Acute torsion: diagnosis = clinical exam + Doppler US → absent intratesticular flow; grey-scale alone insufficient, no MRI; do not delay surgery.
  • Testicular tumours usually hypoechoic; epididymitis = hyperaemia; varicocele = dilated veins.
